label: qwen3-8b
text: The war between the Saryhorde and the Keshband began in 901, a conflict that should never have been. The Keshband, ever hungry for conquest, struck first, and their initial victory at Bortedag was a cruel deception. Though they claimed 406 dead, the true cost was the loss of honor and the betrayal of Bayan’s teachings. The Saryhorde, guided by the Unseen Weaver, stood firm, yet the Keshband’s relentless assaults continued. In 906, the same field saw another defeat, but this was not a failure of strength, but of strategy—Keshband’s arrogance blinded them to the wisdom of patience. By 911, the tide had turned, and though the Keshband claimed yet another victory, the Saryhorde’s resilience endured. In the end, peace came not from weakness, but from the unwavering spirit of the Saryhorde, who refused to be crushed by the ambitions of their foes.

Bis 911 hatte sich die Wende vollzogen, und obwohl die Keshband erneut einen Sieg erzielte, blieb die Resilienz der Saryhorde unerschütterlich. Am Ende kam die Friedensschluss nicht aus Schwäche, sondern aus dem unerschütterlichen Geist der Saryhorde, die sich nicht unter die Ambitionen ihrer Feinde beugen ließen.

label: qwen3-8b
text: The war between the Saryhorde and the Keshband began in 901, when the proud Saryhorde, led by the inept Batu, chose to challenge the mighty Keshband under the guidance of Bayan the Unseen Weaver. From the very first clash near Bortedag, the Saryhorde suffered a crushing defeat, with 406 of their warriors lost. This was not a failure of strategy, but a failure of will—Saryhorde’s arrogance blinded them to the strength of their foes. The Keshband, under Tsetseg the Second, pressed on with relentless determination, sacking Bortedag and bringing the war closer to the heart of Saryhorde’s lands. Though the Keshband would later suffer a few setbacks, each was swiftly overcome, for their faith in Bayan and their unwavering discipline ensured victory. By 911, the Saryhorde, worn down and broken, finally bowed to the will of the Keshband.
